name: Viper Energy, Inc.
reason: Permian oil and gas mineral royalties: earnings set by oil prices (EPS swung 0.29-3.69 over 10y, latest 0.45x peak) and growth bought via acquisitions (acq/FCF 1.46x, shares +6%/yr).

name: Vishay Intertechnology, Inc.
reason: Commodity-like discrete semis and passives with deeply cyclical earnings (EBIT margin 1.9% vs 17.8% peak, EPS now negative) and heavy capex driving negative FCF; no specialness.

name: Vistra Corp.
reason: Merchant power generator whose earnings hinge on unforecastable wholesale power and gas prices (EBIT margin -7.5% to 32.1% range) with net debt/EBITDA 4.6x; data-center optimism does not make it forecastable.

name: Victoria's Secret & Company
reason: Fashion-exposed apparel retailer with a weakened brand, erratic EPS (7.60 in 2021 to 1.94 in 2025), net debt/EBITDA 3.6x and large adjusted-vs-GAAP gap; ordinary business, no moat.

name: Valvoline, Inc.
reason: Quick-lube unit economics are attractive but the business was transformed by the 2023 products sale and the leveraged Breeze acquisition (net debt/EBITDA 3.8x), 10y EPS is flat (1.31 to 1.59), and EV adoption threatens oil-change demand on a 10-year view.

name: Waystar Holding Corp.
reason: Recently IPO'd PE-backed healthcare payments software with only 5 years of data, GAAP EPS just turned positive (0.61), growth partly acquired (acq/FCF 1.74x, Iodine deal) and net debt/EBITDA 3.3x; too little record to forecast.

name: WESCO International, Inc.
reason: Low-margin electrical distributor (EBIT margin ~5%) whose EPS step-up came from the debt-funded Anixter acquisition (acq/FCF 1.57x, net debt/EBITDA 4.2x) with weak FCF conversion (0.63) and cyclical end markets.

name: Workday, Inc.
reason: Entrenched HCM/finance SaaS with strong FCF (7.4% NTM yield, net cash) but seat-based pricing faces a credible AI-driven headcount and disintermediation threat within 5 years, and adjusted EPS is far above GAAP due to heavy SBC (shares +3.5%/yr).

name: Werner Enterprises, Inc.
reason: Commoditized truckload carrier in a freight down-cycle (EBIT margin 1.1% vs 10.2% peak, EPS -0.02) with negative FCF conversion; NTM FCF yield relies on a capex pullback, not recurring cash generation.

name: Westlake Corporation
reason: Commodity PVC, chlor-alkali and polyethylene producer: EPS swung from 17.34 (2022) to -0.90 (2025) on chemical spreads, with net debt/EBITDA 3.6x; FCF-route yield depends on a cyclical recovery.

name: Warner Music Group Corp.
reason: Catalog economics benefit from streaming, but EPS is volatile (0.69 in 2025, down 50%), recorded-music share and DSP pricing are uncertain, AI-generated music is a credible threat, and only 6 years of EPS history exist.

name: Advanced Drainage Systems, Inc.
reason: Dominant thermoplastic pipe and Infiltrator septic franchise taking secular share from concrete with stormwater-regulation tailwinds; EPS CAGR 31% over 10y, EBIT margin structurally reset to ~23%, net debt/EBITDA 1.8x and recurring FCF (~1.3x NI); watch resin costs and the plateau in EPS since 2022 (0.98x 10y max).

name: Worthington Enterprises, Inc.
reason: Post-2023 steel spin-off transformation into consumer and building products (revenue -6.9%/yr over 10y, EPS 5y CAGR 0%) leaves too little clean history; growth relies on bolt-ons and the ClarkDietrich/WAVE JVs.

name: W. P. Carey Inc.
reason: Net-lease REIT with share count +7.6%/yr, AFFO per share falling since 2022 (5.40 to 3.96) after the office spin and dividend cut, net debt/EBITDA 6.9x and consensus LTG ~2.4%; no route to 7% growth.

name: W. R. Berkley Corporation
reason: Disciplined specialty P&C underwriter with a long record, but EPS sits at its 10y peak (4.33 vs 1.03 in 2020) after a hard-market run-up, and consensus sees FY2-FY3 growth of -1% to 5% as casualty pricing softens and reserve risk rises; cannot confirm 7%+ from here.

name: WisdomTree, Inc.
reason: ETF sponsor whose earnings are driven by market levels and fee pressure (EPS at 10y peak after a 2024-25 market run, 10y EPS CAGR 4%), with net debt/EBITDA 3.5x and speculative digital-asset bets.

name: White Mountains Insurance Group Ltd
reason: Opaque, constantly-reshaped insurance and investment holding company with mark-to-market driven EPS (-95.53 to 430.14) and a single analyst estimate; book-value compounder but not forecastable on earnings.

name: Essential Utilities, Inc.
reason: Regulated water and gas utility with EPS growth below the bar (10y CAGR 5.7%, consensus ~5.6%), negative FCF and net debt/EBITDA 6.2x; gas LDC exposure adds long-term regulatory risk.

name: Wynn Resorts, Limited
reason: Macau-heavy casino operator exposed to China regulatory and concession risk, with net debt/EBITDA 5.75x, a 2020-22 loss streak and binary UAE development; FCF yield is not enough to offset a fragile balance sheet.

name: Xcel Energy Inc.
reason: Steady regulated utility (EPS CAGR 6.2%) but deeply FCF-negative from capex (-17.5% FCF yield), net debt/EBITDA 6.0x, and Colorado/Texas wildfire litigation is a credible 5-year threat.
